definitions.explanation: Seasoned pork that is braised or roasted, commonly served as a ramen topping or in rice bowls. Adapted from Chinese char siu.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
From Chinese {叉焼|チャーシャオ} (chāshāo). The Japanese version is typically braised in soy sauce and mirin rather than roasted with a sweet glaze as in Chinese cooking.

USAGE:
In Japan, チャーシュー most commonly refers to pork slices served on ramen. Many ramen shops offer extra チャーシュー as a topping. It is also served over rice as チャーシュー{丼|どん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- チャーシュー⟦{麺|めん}→麺：14644_men⟧: char siu ramen (with extra pork)
- チャーシュー{丼|どん}: char siu rice bowl
- ⟦{自家製|じかせい}→自家製：13947_jikasei⟧チャーシュー: house-made char siu
- ⟦{炙|あぶ}り→炙る：09006_aburu⟧チャーシュー: seared/torched char siu
